verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is that a published Lovable app can be exposed as an MCP server for AI assistants, with configurable tools, sign-in, permissions and access (lovable-docs-8, lovable-docs-26). This suggests some ability to limit what an agent can do, but nothing describes issuing scoped or least-privilege API credentials. Lovable's own MCP server (lovable-docs-37) has no documented token scoping, and the enterprise 'granular access controls' (lovable-docs-46) concern workspace members, not agent credentials. Missing for 10: explicit scoped API key/token issuance, a per-credential permission model, scoping for the Lovable MCP server, credential rotation/revocation, and independent corroboration.
